title: Hormones straight to the blood
objective: Recall the main islet hormones and which cell makes each.

steps.title: The endocrine pancreas
steps.body:
The **[[endocrine]]** pancreas is the **[[islet|islets of Langerhans]]** — tiny cell clusters secreting hormones into the blood (unlike the **[[exocrine]]** acini that secrete enzymes into ducts, D6).

- **[[beta cell|β cells]]** → **[[insulin]]**
- **[[alpha cell|α cells]]** → **[[glucagon]]**
- **δ cells** → **[[somatostatin]]**

steps.prompt: Match each islet cell to its hormone.
steps.explanation: β→insulin (lowers glucose), α→glucagon (raises glucose), δ→somatostatin (a local brake on both).

steps.prompt: What makes the islets **endocrine** rather than exocrine?
options: They secrete hormones into the blood, not into ducts
They release hormones into the pancreatic duct
They make and release the main digestive enzymes
They have essentially no blood supply of their own
steps.explanation: Endocrine = into the bloodstream. The islets are richly vascularized so their hormones reach the whole body.

variants.setup: Islet hormones need to reach distant tissues like muscle and liver.
options: Through the bloodstream, the endocrine route
Down the pancreatic duct to the intestine
Along motor nerves out toward the tissues
variants.reveal: Islets secrete into the blood — the endocrine route — so hormones reach distant organs.

steps.title: A small but vital minority
steps.body: Islets are only ~1–2% of the pancreas by mass, yet they run whole-body glucose control. The exocrine 98% and this endocrine sliver can fail independently — a theme from D6 that matters for diabetes.

reviewNotes: Islet hormones recap; builds on D6.
